title: Firmware tag ordering (epochs, channels, hotfix post-releases) and ~/^ constraints with pre-release gating

hidden_checks.spec: Rule 2: dev < alpha < beta < rc < final < hotfix; hotfix sorts after the final release. Rule 4: all six operators.
Rule 2: channel numbers compare numerically (rc.2 < rc.10).
Rule 2: a channel written without a number has number 0 (1.0-rc == 1.0-rc.0).
Rule 1: compare (major, minor, patch) before phase.
Rule 1: epoch first (higher epoch is always newer); epoch defaults to 0 (grammar).
Rule 3: build metadata and v prefix never affect ordering or equality; missing patch is 0; equal versions have equal hashes.
Rule 4: comparing with a non-Version returns NotImplemented (== is False, ordering raises TypeError).
Rule 11: new list of the tag strings exactly as given, ascending; equal versions keep input order.
Rule 11: an invalid tag raises fwver.InvalidVersion.
Rule 5: no operator means ==.
Rule 6: comparison clauses use the ordering, so ==1.2 matches 1.2.0+b3; satisfies accepts a Version.
Rule 5: a version satisfies a spec only if it satisfies every clause; != operator.
Rule 5: whitespace around clauses and between operator and version is ignored.
Rule 6: <=1.2.0 does not match 1.2.0-hotfix.1; rule 9: hotfix versions match normally.
Rule 5: empty spec, empty clause, unknown operator or invalid tag in a clause raises InvalidConstraint (a ValueError subclass).
API: a bad tag string passed as version raises fwver.InvalidVersion.
Rule 8: ^V is >=V and < (major+1).0.0 when major > 0.
Rule 8: 0.(minor+1).0 when major == 0; no special case for 0.0.x (^0.0.3 means >=0.0.3,<0.1.0).
Rules 7/8: upper bound has the same epoch as V; rule 1 epoch dominates.
Rule 9: pre-releases never match unless a clause names a pre-release of the same release (^1.4.0 does not match 2.0.0-rc.1; >=1.0 does not match 1.5.0-rc.1).
Rule 9: >=1.5.0-beta matches 1.5.0-rc.1 and not 1.6.0-alpha.
Rule 9: the clause pre-release must have the same epoch, major, minor and patch.
Rule 9: at least one clause's tag (any clause) is a pre-release with the same release.
Rule 9: hotfix versions are not pre-releases and match normally.
Rule 10: returns the tag string exactly as given of the highest satisfying version; invalid tags ignored.
Rule 10: when several satisfying tags are equal versions, the first in tags wins.
Rule 10: ignores invalid tags; returns None if none satisfies.
Rule 10: an invalid spec raises InvalidConstraint even for an empty tags.
